editorial:
Imagine being a housewife in a small village where everyone tells you to just stay in the kitchen. That is exactly where you find Chandro and Prakashi. These two women are tired of the boring routine and the way men treat them, so they decide to pick up guns and learn how to shoot. It is a wild and heartwarming ride that feels like a big celebration of spirit. You will love how they go from being underestimated locals to world-class shooters, all while dealing with grumpy husbands and skeptical neighbors. The vibe is light, funny, and really inspiring, making you want to cheer for them every single second.

Bhumi Pednekar and Taapsee Pannu are fantastic here, bringing a lot of energy and humor to their roles. The pacing is quick, and the scenes where they train are genuinely exciting to watch. While some parts feel a bit like a typical sports movie, the real-life story makes it feel special. If you want a feel-good movie for the whole family, you should definitely check this out.
endingExplained: The movie ends with the two women overcoming all the odds and the people who doubted them. After years of hard work and facing a lot of pushback from their community, they finally compete on a global stage. They prove their skill by winning major shooting championships, becoming the oldest sharpshooters in the world. It wraps up with them gaining the respect of their husbands and village, showing that it is never too late to follow your dreams.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves true stories about underdogs winning against the odds.
